description: Codify the CAM Runtime brand palette (4 greens + 5 neutrals) as named design tokens in src/design/tokens.ts, keeping the figure-only subagent colors out of the chrome tokens.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Ink's <Text color> prop accepts raw hex strings (e.g. color="#005cc5") because Ink delegates color handling to chalk; named colors and rgb() are also supported. Confirms the brand palette can be stored as raw hex token values and consumed directly by the splash (CAM-329) via Ink color props, exactly as the existing palette tokens already are. No breaking changes or deprecations affecting this scope.

userStories.title: Codify the CAM Runtime brand palette as named design tokens
userStories.description: As a designer of CAM Runtime surfaces, I need the brand palette (greens + neutrals) available as named, documented design tokens in the one design-token module, so the splash accent (CAM-329) and the README brand (CAM-331) reference a single source instead of inlining raw hexes.
acceptanceCriteria: src/design/tokens.ts exports the four brand greens as NAMED tokens with a semantic name and a per-token usage note: Fir Green #10C66F (primary accent: subscribe button, links, nav, highlights), Forest Green #003333 (deep green: text over green surfaces), Aero Green #CAFFE3 (light green: welcome background, light highlight), White #FFFFFF (base). [oracle: file-assert grep -q '#10C66F' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#003333' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#CAFFE3' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#FFFFFF' src/design/tokens.ts]

src/design/tokens.ts exports the five brand neutrals as NAMED tokens with a semantic name and a per-token usage note: #1F1F1F (ink: dark text/backgrounds, tiles, dark cards, banner), #6F6F6F (secondary text), #9C9C9C (secondary over dark), #EDECF0 (surface: light cards/surfaces), #E3E3E5 (line: borders/dividers). [oracle: file-assert grep -q '#1F1F1F' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#6F6F6F' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#9C9C9C' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#EDECF0' src/design/tokens.ts && grep -q '#E3E3E5' src/design/tokens.ts]

The brand tokens are exported SEPARATELY from the existing chrome `palette` export (which keeps its semantic status roles), so importing brand identity never force-restyles a status surface. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'export const palette' src/design/tokens.ts]

The four subagent-marking colors (Blue Lotus #426DFF, Lemon #AFE220, Sun Yellow #FFDF24, Salmon #FF6666) are FIGURE-ONLY and therefore absent from src/design/tokens.ts entirely (values AND prose): a comment in the module states that the subagent figure colors are deliberately not chrome tokens and points to the CONTEXT.md brand terms as their canonical home, WITHOUT restating the hex values. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE '426DFF|AFE220|FFDF24|FF6666' src/design/tokens.ts]

A test guards the figure-only exclusion by asserting that none of the four subagent hex values appear in any exported token of the design-token module (mirroring the negative oracle above, so a future leak into chrome fails the suite). [oracle: bun test test/design/tokens.test.ts]

No existing color usage is force-migrated: the chrome accent stays #4EBE7D and src/ui/theme.ts, src/logging/color.ts, src/ui/Section.tsx and src/logging/screen.ts are not modified by this story. [oracle: file-assert grep -q '#4EBE7D' src/design/tokens.ts && git diff --name-only main -- src/ui/theme.ts src/logging/color.ts src/ui/Section.tsx src/logging/screen.ts | wc -l | grep -q '^ *0$']

The palette and its usage rules are already recorded as durable brand documentation in the CONTEXT.md brand terms on main (Fir Green / Forest Green / Aero Green / brand neutrals / subagent colors), written by the deterministic domain-docs writer; this story does NOT hand-edit CONTEXT.md. [oracle: file-assert git show main:CONTEXT.md | grep -q '10C66F' && git show main:CONTEXT.md | grep -q '426DFF']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
The full quality spine is green (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes:
Files: src/design/tokens.ts (add the brand export next to the existing `palette`/`glyphs`/`layout` exports; keep the module dependency-free -- no `ink`, no `chalk` imports, per its header contract), plus a NEW test/design/tokens.test.ts (the test/design/ directory does not exist yet; test/ mirrors source). DO NOT touch src/ui/theme.ts (re-exports `palette` as `colors`) or src/logging/color.ts (wraps palette in chalk.hex): the issue forbids a force-restyle, and the existing chrome palette (accent #4EBE7D, warning #FFCB1F, destructive #F25F5C, muted #808080) is a SEPARATE concern from brand identity -- brand green #10C66F is NOT the status-accent green, so do not collapse the two exports.

ORDERING (coordinated at plan time, per the issue's gotcha): CAM-329 (uppercase splash + Fir Green splash accent) is still OPEN/unshipped as of planning, so THIS issue lands the Fir Green token FIRST and CAM-329 consumes it; wiring src/ui/Splash.tsx is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here (CAM-329 owns that surface and its wordmark rewrite). Do not edit Splash.tsx.

CONTEXT.md: the brand terms are ALREADY on main (commit e4248f3f, `docs(cam): domain docs for CAM-332`, all greens/neutrals/subagent colors with usage rules). CONTEXT.md is writer-owned (populated via the CAM-118 deterministic writer `writeDomainDocsOnMain`, src/commands/domain-docs.ts, committed ref-only to main) and is glossary-only: do NOT hand-edit it on this branch -- a hand-edit both duplicates existing content and collides with the on-main writer channel. The doc AC is a file-assert against main, not work.

GOTCHA (patterns.md, US-002/CAM-149 2026-07-05, negative-grep oracles): the AC bans the substrings 426DFF|AFE220|FFDF24|FF6666 ANYWHERE in src/design/tokens.ts, including comments and docstrings. When writing the 'subagent figure colors are not chrome tokens' comment, describe them by NAME only (Blue Lotus / Lemon / Sun Yellow / Salmon) and point at CONTEXT.md; never restate a hex value, or the oracle trips exactly as a real leak would.

Docs (Step 5.5 re-check): Ink consumes these tokens as raw hex via `<Text color="#10C66F">` (Ink delegates to chalk, so hex/named/rgb all work) -- https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink#color. Tokens stay raw hex strings, `as const`, matching the existing palette shape; no CSS.

Test quality (curated invariant): tokens.ts is pure data, so assert real exported values plus a real read of the module file for the absence guard -- no mocks, no tautological mock-call assertions.
